about: webcpp::hash's measured table, a reference measured once, on 2026-11-16, that decides nothing: the size of one program per cell of doc/capabilities.json on each target, and its throughput. Every key derivation's default is backends::hash2, argon2id's and scrypt's backends::sodium, whatever this table says (spec section 4.1); no lane measures it again. Written by the superproject's tools/hash/measure.py --write (webcpp at 76b1730), from the programs of webcpp::hash's test/measure (hash at 46b1989), both since retired; tools/hash/doc_tables.py renders doc/measurements.adoc from it.

layout.schema: This description. The version of the layout is "version"; a change of layout raises it. "digest" is the SHA-256 of the file without it, which tools/hash/doc_tables.py --check checks, so that the reference is never edited by hand.
layout.date, machine, load_average_before_after: when and where the measurements were made; loaded says whether the machine was shared and loaded
layout.toolchains, runtimes, strip, pins, build: the compiler per target, wasmtime and node, the strip of the native sizes, each backend's library and pin (from doc/capabilities.json), and the two builds
layout.native_toolchain: what the native rows were measured with: the compiler, the host's operating system and processor, and the strip
layout.workloads: per function, what one computation does (spec 4.2)
layout.records[]: one per cell and target: operation (the function of doc/capabilities.json), hmac (or null), backend, target, size_bytes, result (the hexadecimal output, the same for every backend and target of an operation and hmac), throughput (repetitions, invocations, runs_per_invocation, invocation_medians_ns, median_ns, min_ns, max_ns: nanoseconds per computation) or null with throughput_absent saying why. operation, hmac, backend and target are the keys of doc/measurements.throughput.json's cases too, which the documentation joins on them; constant time is doc/capabilities.json's.
layout.orders[]: per operation, hmac and target: by_size and by_throughput, the backends that have it there in order, and throughput_from, the target whose throughput ordered it, as measured; they order nothing in the library
layout.rules: how sizes, throughput and orders are made

pins.hash2: Boost.Hash2 1.92, and webcpp's own HKDF and PBKDF2 over its hmac<H>

rules.size: the bytes of the program built at variant=release optimization=space: natively the executable stripped with strip, on WebAssembly the .wasm file, which carries no debug information
rules.throughput: the program built at variant=release optimization=speed, run with --time: one computation to warm up, then five timed runs of the workload, each repeated `repetitions` times; per invocation the median of its five runs, per record the median of its invocations' medians, with the fastest and slowest run
rules.order: spec 4.2: by size, the smallest program first; by throughput, the lowest median of the invocations' medians first, a committed order changing only where a median is more than 10 percent below the median of the backend ahead of it; on a first measurement, the medians alone (an exact tie keeps the capability table's order of backends). A WebAssembly target orders by its own throughput where every backend of the row ran within the bound, else by the native order. The native orders hold for the native toolchain that measured them (native_toolchain); the lane compares them only on that toolchain.
rules.loaded: the larger of the two 1-minute load averages exceeds the core count
